chunks.text: Which is more important for training data, consistency or diversity? If you aim at medium SR, keeping consistent is OK; if you want very high SR, then diversity is necessary.

chunks.text: If using only the current frame, the robot is easier to get stuck. If using history frames, the robot can be more confident, but the model is easier to get overfitted. It is suggested to use the current frame and the history frame one action chunk earlier. For example, if the action horizon is 40, set the video delta indices to [-40, 0].
chunks.title: only current frame robot easier get stuck. history

chunks.text: GR00T N1.7 supports additional observation history via delta_indices (state or image or both). You will find an explanation in https://github.com/NVIDIA/Isaac-GR00T/blob/main/getting_started/data_config.md. We recommend adding video/image observation history for your task, before experimenting further with action_prefix conditioning. The reason is that N1.7 was trained with mixed
chunks.title: GR00T N1.7 supports additional observation history delta indices

chunks.text: Finally, we recommend verifying that the control stack used during data collection matches deployment as closely as possible, including IK solver, low-level controller, control frequency, action representation, and any smoothing or filtering.
chunks.title: Finally recommend verifying control stack during data collection

chunks.text: We recommend starting with video/image history only. State history can be tried afterward, but some internal experiments found that adding state history can make the model more likely to overfit.

chunks.text: stiff control is preferable if possible, easier to learn as reducing latency

chunks.text: When collecting data by tele-op, look at camera images but not the real robot. Make sure you see what the robot sees. It may affect speed and quality at the beginning, but will be fine after some practice.

chunks.text: Especially since you wrote your own trainers, you should make sure to recompute post-training dataset stats (see flag in https://github.com/NVIDIA/Isaac-GR00T/blob/main/gr00t/configs/data/data_config.py#L76). In the Isaac-GR00T repo, the flag controls whether the dataset stats computed from your finetuning dataset should replace the normalization stats baked into the pretrained checkpoint. You should make sure the recomputed stats are used during training and inference.

chunks.text: GR00T N1.7 result sharing: Compared with N1.6, N1.7 performs much better on instruction-following and robustness tasks, and is roughly similar for manipulation tasks.
chunks.title: GR00T N1.7 result sharing Compared N1.6 performs better

chunks.text: You are collecting data in real and evaluating in Sim. It is important for the Sim environment to accurately reflect the real environment. It is worth testing if the policy works well, if trained on data collected in Sim, but also validating performance on the real setup.
chunks.title: collecting data real evaluating Sim. important Sim environment

chunks.text: N1.7 supports relative action representations, and we recommend checking whether your 29D action vector should be configured as relative actions where applicable, if not yet. See getting_started/finetune_new_embodiment.md for guidance on configuring relative EEF for your robot. Representing actions as deltas from the current pose (rather than absolute targets) improves generalization and is a key factor in the model's cross-embodiment performance.
chunks.title: N1.7 supports relative action representations recommend checking whether

chunks.text: If the task is not common or unseen in pretraining, you better turn on tune_llm and tune_visual to finetune parameters in the LLM backbone and vision encoder. In that case, you should use a lower LR than tuning the action head only. It will use more GPU memories.

chunks.text: fail + retry behavior in data collection: avoid them, or only keep recovered parts (dagger, annotate good/bad intervals, only train with good)

chunks.text: When collecting DAgger data, use the human trajectory only and discard the robot trajectory, because the robot trajectory leads the robot to a bad state. We do not want the model to imitate bad robot trajectories.

chunks.text: For difficult tasks, first manage to reach a 20-30% success rate. Once you reach that, then you can try DAgger to improve further.

chunks.text: Short horizon in inference is good for action precision, while long horizon is good for action continuity.

chunks.text: It is not recommended to start with UMI data in post-training, because there is an embodiment gap between the 3rd-party UMI gloves and your robot.

chunks.text: If it is a new embodiment and unseen task, you can try two-stage training. First, turn off tune_llm and tune_visual and train action head only, it helps the action head to warm up on the new action space. Then turn on tune_llm and tune_visual, it helps the model to better adapt to the new task. If you turn on all parameters from the beginning, the action can be very noisy and may cause loss spikes.
